NAT_DATA 1 km planning units for an area of interest

Source: R/natdata.R
create_1km_grid.Rd

Makes the 1 km planning units of an area of interest (AOI) on the national template of a NAT_DATA folder (ConsTech's shared national data): the AOI in the template's CRS, a raster of the AOI's cells holding each cell's national ID, and one square polygon per cell with its national ID (NCCID) and a planning-unit number (PUID). It is the first step of building a Where To Work project, and the defaults give the planning units wtw-data-prep2 makes. Nothing is written.

Usage

create_1km_grid(
  aoi,
  natdata_dir,
  cells = "touches",
  value = "NCCID",
  id = "PUID",
  index = "template",
  order = "value"
)

Arguments

aoi

The AOI: anything read_aoi() accepts (sf, sfc or SpatVector polygons, a file path, or bounds with their CRS in an sf bbox). Several polygons are dissolved into one.

natdata_dir

The NAT_DATA folder: a single path to an existing folder, such as a dated release (NAT_DATA_20261009). Its template is opened with natdata_template() (_1km/idx.tif). Where NAT_DATA lives is each tool's own setting; this function only reads from it.

cells

The cell inclusion rule, one of "touches" (every cell the AOI touches) or "centre" (every cell whose centre is inside the AOI). The default, "touches", gives the cells wtw-data-prep2 gives.

value

The name of the column of national IDs in the polygons, and of the raster's layer: a single, non-empty string. The default, "NCCID", is NAT_DATA's name.

id

NULL or the name of a column that numbers the polygons 1 to n in their order (see order): a single, non-empty string, different from value. The default, "PUID", is the planning-unit ID of Where To Work projects. NULL adds none.

index

What the national ID (value) is, one of:

  • "template" (the default): the template's value in each cell. In NAT_DATA, _1km/idx.tif numbers its cells row by row from the bottom-left cell; this is the shared national ID that wtw-data-prep2 writes as NCCID and other tools join on.

  • "cell": the cell's number in the template in terra's numbering (row by row from the top-left cell, starting at 1), which links each cell directly to the columns of NAT_DATA's rij matrices.

order

The order of the polygons, and so of id, one of:

  • "value" (the default): sorted by national ID (value), smallest first, as wtw-data-prep2 orders them.

  • "cell": terra's cell order (row by row from the top-left cell), as polygonize_raster() returns them.

With index = "cell" the two orders are the same.

Value

A list, with nothing written:

  • aoi: the AOI as read_aoi() returns it, an sf data frame with one polygon or multipolygon and no attributes, in the template's CRS;

  • aoi_raster: a SpatRaster with one layer named value, on the template's grid (cropped to the AOI): the national ID in the AOI's cells and NA elsewhere. It can be passed as the aoi_raster of extract_layers() and clip_rij_matrix(), which use only which cells are not NA;

  • polygons: an sf data frame with one POLYGON row per AOI cell, in the template's CRS, with the columns value (the national ID, as in the raster: an integer for NAT_DATA's idx.tif and for index = "cell", a double for a template that stores floats), id (an integer, 1 to n) unless id = NULL, and geometry.

Method

  1. Template: natdata_template() opens natdata_dir's _1km/idx.tif (1 km cells in Canada_Albers_WGS_1984); its values stay on disk.

  2. AOI: read_aoi() in the template's CRS, dissolved into one polygon; reprojection, when needed, moves each vertex with PROJ.

  3. Cells: rasterize_aoi() on the template at its own resolution, with cells, raster (not vector) intersection: "touches" is GDAL's all-touched rule, "centre" cell centres inside the AOI. AOI cells where the template has no data (NA, off the national template's land) are dropped. The raster is cropped to the AOI's bounding box, snapped out to whole cells, and holds the national ID (index) in the AOI's cells and NA elsewhere.

  4. Polygons: polygonize_raster(), one square polygon per AOI cell (cells are not merged), holding the same national ID as the raster. The national ID keeps the template's type (ADR 0019): an integer if the template stores integers (an INT* data type, as NAT_DATA's idx.tif does) and a double if it stores floats. Terra cell numbers (index = "cell") are always integers.

  5. Order: with order = "value", the polygons are sorted by national ID, then id numbers them 1 to n.

No areas are computed and no values are rounded. With the defaults, the cells, NCCID, PUID and polygons are those of wtw-data-prep2's create_1km_grid(), which reached the "touches" rule through a 1000 m buffer and a mask. Unlike it, the raster holds the national IDs, not 1s, on the AOI's extent, and the polygons' columns are value, id and then geometry. Decisions are recorded in ADR 0008, ADR 0017 and ADR 0019.

If the AOI's bounding box does not overlap the template, the function stops with an error. If it overlaps but gets no cells, it warns, and the raster is all NA and the polygons have no rows.

See also

rasterize_aoi() and polygonize_raster(), the building blocks it calls.

Other natdata: natdata_template(), read_natdata_metadata()

Examples

# A small NAT_DATA-like folder: its _1km/idx.tif is a 10 x 10 template
natdata_dir <- system.file("extdata", "natdata", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

grid <- create_1km_grid(aoi, natdata_dir)
grid$polygons
#> Simple feature collection with 9 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   NCCID PUID                       geometry
#> 1    34    1 POLYGON ((1003000 606000, 1...
#> 2    35    2 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 3    36    3 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 4    44    4 POLYGON ((1003000 605000, 1...
#> 5    45    5 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 6    46    6 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 7    54    7 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
#> 8    55    8 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 9    56    9 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...
terra::values(grid$aoi_raster, mat = FALSE)
#> [1] 34 35 36 44 45 46 54 55 56

# Only cells whose centre is inside the AOI, in terra's cell order,
# without planning-unit numbers
create_1km_grid(
  aoi, natdata_dir,
  cells = "centre", id = NULL, order = "cell"
)$polygons
#> Simple feature collection with 6 features and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1004000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   NCCID                       geometry
#> 1    35 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 2    36 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 3    45 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 4    46 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 5    55 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 6    56 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...

# Terra cell numbers as the ID (the example template's values are its cell
# numbers, so here they are the same as the default's)
create_1km_grid(aoi, natdata_dir, index = "cell")$polygons$NCCID
#> [1] 34 35 36 44 45 46 54 55 56
